title: Prospective audit and feedback for antimicrobial stewardship: a two-strand scoping review for extending the service
subtitle: Measured outcomes and experience of recommendations, charted as separate strands
statement: A three-hospital network runs prospective audit and feedback on the teaching hospital's medical wards and must decide in April 2027 whether and how to extend it to surgery, intensive care and two community hospitals with the same staff. Committee members disagree on whether the case rests on measured outcomes or on how prescribers receive feedback. A scoping review will map both kinds of evidence as separate strands, each with its own question and main result, without pooling.
whoAffected: Inpatients exposed to unnecessary broad-spectrum antimicrobials, especially in surgery and intensive care; prescribers, pharmacists and nurses who give and receive recommendations; the two community hospitals without on-site stewardship; and the committee.
whatHurts: Unnecessary antimicrobial days drive resistance, C. difficile and adverse effects; recommendations that are ignored waste scarce pharmacist time; extending the service badly could spread staff too thin everywhere.
currentPractice: Day-3 pharmacist review with written recommendations on medical wards, handshake rounds twice a week on two wards, and telephone advice only for the community hospitals.
whyNow: The committee decides in April 2027 and has asked for a written summary by 31 March; the surgical try-out showed low acceptance of written recommendations.
constraints: No budget; four pharmacist hours a week to March 2027; second screener from January; fellow two hours a week; summary by 31 March 2027; two strands reported separately; English and French.
patientCenteredGoal: Patients in every ward and hospital of the network receive the antimicrobials they need for as long as they need them, and no longer.
summary: Problem framed as a two-strand scoping question to inform the extension of audit and feedback.
